Three places that hold water

01 / Main source

Inverted bottle

Holds most of the unheated water and supplies the machine through its seat.

02 / Branch point

Reservoir below the bottle

Holds unheated water and supplies both the ambient outlet and heated tank.

03 / Heating and storage

Separate hot tank

Stores and heats a portion of water. During dispensing, water enters below and leaves above.

REHEATING / EVAPORATION / STORAGE

What matters when water is left standing?

Separate three processes: thermostat reheating, concentration of existing solutes, and storage hygiene. A heating count alone does not establish whether water is safe.

01 / Thermostat cycle

Stored water can reheat

With the dispensing valves closed, water stays in the hot tank. The thermostat switches heating according to temperature. This differs from continuous boiling.

Repeated-boiling experiments found that changes in water quality are mainly driven by source composition and evaporation concentration. They do not establish safety for every source or storage condition, nor does another heating cycle prove excessive nitrite.

Zhai et al., Journal of Water and Health, 2020
02 / Existing solutes

Less water can mean higher concentration

Existing nonvolatile solutes may remain as water evaporates. EPA explains that boiling does not remove nitrate; evaporation can increase its concentration.

Relative concentration 1.25× C / C₀ = V₀ / V

Teaching model: no refill or dispensing; solutes do not evaporate, react or precipitate. Dots represent the relative amount of existing solute. A real tank refills and dispenses, so this model does not predict its actual concentration. The ratio is not a safety threshold.

EPA: boiling does not remove nitrate
03 / Storage and hygiene

Heating the tank does not heat every water path

The upper reservoir, ambient branch and spouts do not undergo hot-tank heating. Research on bottled-water dispensers links microbial conditions to storage, use, cleaning and maintenance.

WHO describes microbial reduction of nitrate to nitrite under suitable conditions. This conditional mechanism does not establish that it occurred in this machine or exceeded a limit.

Tischner et al., Pathogens, 2021 WHO: nitrate and nitrite, 2022

Prioritise water source and cleaning

Use a suitable water source and follow the bottle label and dispenser instructions for storage and cleaning. After long disuse, replace water and clean as directed before restarting. Suspected nitrate or other chemical contamination calls for checking water quality or changing the source, not additional boiling.

CDC: drinking water and maintenance

This page explains mechanisms and published evidence. No sample from this YR-5-A was tested. The figure cannot establish chemical or microbial concentrations, or a universal number of days after which bottled water becomes unsafe.

Evidence and scope

The owner confirmed YR-5-A, hot/ambient outlets and no separate kettle. The exterior follows the provided photograph; hidden placement follows comparable mechanisms. No factory teardown drawing was available.

  1. CN2539462Y: distribution reservoir and branches: only the ambient/hot topology is used.
  2. CN205963801U: conventional dispenser arrangement: upper distribution reservoir, lower tank inlet and upper outlet.
  3. CN223041337U: bottle-seat air admission and refill: water sealing and air admission at the bottle neck.
  4. CN201510145U: heated tank and thermostat: heater and temperature control.

No refrigeration, filtration or sterilisation system is depicted. Scale, part counts and animation timing support explanation; they are not measurements or a factory bill of materials.
